Menu

How to play

Tap a section to open it.

Joining a race

Enter your race code

Your host will share a race code (or an invite link). Enter it on the Team page to find the race.

Pick a team name and PIN

Choose a team name and set a PIN. You can also pin an avatar for your team, but that part is optional.

Logging back in

Your race code, team name and PIN are your login. Use them to sign in on another device, or if you ever get logged out.

Wait for approval

Once you have joined, your host gets a notification to approve your team. You are in the race as soon as they do.

The Team page

Your race at a glance

Once you are in, the Team page has four main areas:

  • Race start – where you start your race or hunt. If your host has enabled global start, they will start every team remotely.
  • Time – your running clock.
  • Bonus – any bonus rewards or time deductions you have earned.
  • Checkpoints achieved – how many stops you have completed.

Your journey so far

Shows your chosen route at a glance, your next stop, and the time since your last stop.

Checkpoints

Make the route yours

Your checkpoint list can be reorganised to suit your preferred route. Press and hold a card, then drag it into place.

Tap a card for more

Tapping a checkpoint shows fun facts and, depending on your race’s difficulty level, hints and/or a map of where the checkpoint is.

Guide

The guide button opens compass navigation to help you home in as you close in on your checkpoint.

Check in

Check in completes the checkpoint.

Too far away? Manual check in

If the app thinks you are too far from the checkpoint but you are sure you are in the right place, you can do a manual check in. Your host can review and reject it, so take photo evidence of where you are!

Transit questions

After checking in, if you have left an area or park, you may be asked which transit system you used. If you used more than one (for example a boat and a bus), select them all.

Bonus games

Below your checkpoints

Any bonus games your host has enabled appear below your checkpoint list. They might include:

  • Photo challenge – complete the challenges for time deductions or bonuses.
  • Hidden Mickey bingo – photograph hidden Mickeys to complete your bingo card. Your host may have chosen bingo rules where only one team can win the reward.
  • Wildcard – a random photo challenge is issued for a limited time. The first team to complete it wins.
  • Checkpoint frenzy – the team that completes the most check ins during a set time wins an extra bonus.
  • Trivia – after checking in you may be asked a trivia question. Answer wisely: correct answers earn time deductions.
  • Poison apple – leave your one apple at a stop after you check in. The next team to check in there has to beat a quick mini-game, and the result changes both teams’ times.

The other pages

Race

Leaderboards and live chat live here. Chat is moderated by your host. Badges and rewards also appear here once the race has finished.

Maps

Park maps to help you navigate and plan your journey.

Rules

Get familiar with the rules and options your host has enabled before you set off.

Getting set up

Host login

Open the Host page and register or sign in with your email and password. This is separate from any team login.

New Race / Hunt

The big gold button starts a step-by-step wizard:

  • Name your race or hunt.
  • Mode – a Speed Race (fastest time wins) or a Scavenger Hunt (points).
  • Difficulty – Easy (pins and transit), Medium (park lands) or Hard (blind).
  • Checkpoints – pick them yourself, or let the app choose randomly or by area.
  • Trivia, bonuses and wildcard – choose which extras to switch on.
  • Rules – start from Casual or Competitive, or build your own, and add your own rules for players.
  • Fine-tune – set the missed checkpoint penalty and what teams can see, such as chat, bonuses and live timers.

You can also register a team for yourself if you are playing too.

Share your race code

When the wizard finishes you will get a race code and a share button. Send it to your teams so they can join.

Running your race

Active Races

Every race you have created is listed under Active Races. Open one to see its teams and open its full-screen control panel. Copy or share the race code and delete the race from the top of that panel.

Approving teams

When a team joins, you get a pending approval notice with a Review now button that jumps to that team. Approve them to let them into the race. The notice disappears once nobody is waiting.

Race Controls

Start the race, either for everyone at once with global start or team by team, and manage the race while it is running.

Reviewing teams

Open a team to see their check ins with GPS timestamps, bonus photo proofs and trivia answers. If a manual check in does not look right, you can reject it.

Settings and extras

Race Portal Controls

Choose what teams can see: hide bonuses, hide live timers (the leaderboard ranks by stops only until the finish), and switch live chat on or off. You can also reveal the final results when you are ready and view and moderate the photo gallery.

Race Options

Change the base difficulty and switch trivia, wildcards, Hidden Mickey bingo and checkpoint frenzy on or off, along with their rewards and timings. There is a button to fire a wildcard straight away for testing.

Fair Play Host Lock

Worried about peeking? Nominate a team to hold a PIN. They lock your host panel from their phone, and only they can unlock it again.

After the race

Final results appear automatically once every approved team has finished, or when you reveal them. Teams get their report cards, awards and a photo gallery.

Support

Stuck, found a bug, or got an idea? We’re happy to help.

Email us

Quick fixes

Logged out?

Sign back in with your race code, team name and PIN on the Team page. It works on any device.

Check in not working?

GPS can drift, especially near buildings. If you are sure you are in the right place, use a manual check in and take a photo as evidence. Your host can review it.

Waiting to get in?

Your host has to approve your team before you can race. Let them know you have joined.

Rules

Read carefully before starting your journey across Disney property!

General rules

This page explains how the game works in general. Each host chooses their own settings, so the exact rules for transport, internet use, penalties and special challenges are shown here once you join a race.

Objective

Complete checkpoints according to your race mode (Speed Race vs Scavenger Hunt). Your final adjusted score or time determines your ranking.

Transportation

Your host decides which transportation is allowed, anywhere from walking only to free park transit, paid options like taxis, or any mode at all. The rules for your race will appear here once you join.

Checkpoint Order & Final Location

Checkpoints can be completed in any order you choose, unless your host has designated a specific ending location for a Speed Race. If a final ending location is chosen, it must be completed last so everyone finishes together.

Penalties

In a Speed Race, skipping a required checkpoint adds a time penalty to your final score. Your host sets the size of the penalty (60 minutes unless they change it). In a Scavenger Hunt there are no time penalties, but skipped checkpoints earn no points.

Bonus Challenges

Bonus checkpoints are entirely optional and will improve your overall standings. There are no penalties for missing bonus checkpoints.

Special Challenges

Depending on your host's settings, a race may include extras such as trivia questions, surprise wildcard bonuses, checkpoint frenzies and Hidden Mickey Bingo. If your race uses them, their rules appear on this page after you join.

🧩 Riddle clues

🐭 Hidden Mickey Bingo

Route Planning & Internet Use

Your host decides whether internet help is allowed: none at all, maps and the park app only, or anything goes. The rules for your race will appear here once you join.

Host's Additional Rules

GPS Verification & Discrepancies

When checking in, your device GPS will verify your proximity to the location. If you attempt a check-in but your GPS registers you out of the zone, your entry will be flagged as an override and logged for host review.

🐭 Hidden Mickey Bingo

A 2x2 card where teams photograph four hidden Mickeys. Finish the whole card for a big reward

Speed Race: minutes taken off the final time. Scavenger Hunt: bonus points. An incomplete card earns nothing. Teams submit a photo of a hidden Mickey for each of the four squares.

Trivia Challenge

Ask a question at check-in for bonus rewards

Scavenger Hunt: points. Speed Race: minutes deducted.

Wildcard Challenge

One surprise bonus offered to every team at a random moment

Scavenger Hunt: points. Speed Race: minutes deducted.

Adds a brand-new bonus challenge (on top of any bonuses you chose) from a park where the race already has stops. The first team to submit a photo wins it. It appears automatically (the host can't trigger or cancel it). Speed Race and untimed hunts: after every team has done 2 stops and before anyone has fewer than 2 left. Timed hunts: never in the first or last 15 minutes. If the window passes, it is cancelled.

Checkpoint Frenzy

A surprise race event. Most valid checkpoint check-ins during the frenzy wins.

Scavenger Hunt: points. Speed Race: minutes deducted.

Triggers randomly after every team has completed at least 2 checkpoints and before any team has fewer than 2 left. It will never overlap the wildcard. If the race ends early, valid check-ins up to the final team's finish still count.

🧩 Riddle clues

Up to 1 in 3 stops are shown as a riddle instead of a name. Teams solve it to find where to go, and the name is revealed when they check in.

Hard shows only the riddle. Medium adds the park. Easy adds the park, the area and the map. Only stops that have a riddle written for them can become riddles.

🍎 Poison Apple

Sabotage! Each team gets one apple to leave at a checkpoint for another team to fall into.

After a check-in a team can leave its apple there. The next team to check in at that stop must beat a quick mini-game (catch apples, unscramble words, spot the differences or pick the right antidote). Beat it: they get a 5 minute deduction and the team that left it takes a 5 minute penalty. Fail it: the team that left it gets a 10 minute deduction, and the failing team is not penalised again. (Scavenger Hunts use points instead of minutes.) A team can fall for at most 2 apples, and a stop holds at most 2 waiting apples. An apple nobody triggers in time expires and goes back to its owner to play again.
